title: From the Besieged Singhs’ Misery to the Episode of Banda Singh’s Capture

blocks.text: Observers were shaken by the emaciated bodies of the Singhs, whose condition looked like death before their death. The author presents the siege misery as something almost beyond narration, because hunger, weakness, and confinement had already consumed the defenders while they still lived.

At the same time rumors spread about Banda Singh's survival, because nobody had seen him eat or drink and yet he still endured. That mystery gave rise to wonder as well as fear, making his bodily persistence part of the story even before formal capture was described.

The page then marks a hinge into the next narrative unit by naming the Episode of Banda Singh's Capture. It closes the starvation sequence and explicitly opens the account of how the besieged leader was finally taken.
